handbook-papermakingpapyrus:papyrusmakin:
Papyrus making
Papyrus sheets are made by cutting, soaking, layering, and pressing papyrus pith.

Hold papyrus tops in your active hand and a knife in your offhand, then hold rightmouse to cut the pith into strips. Seal the dry strips in a barrel with 0.5 litres of water per strip for 12 hours.

Place 8 soaked strips on the ground, then add 2 planks and a stone to press them. Leave the pile to dry for about one day. Drying pauses in freezing weather.

When the papyrus is ready, collect the finished sheet with an empty hand.
